item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine has stepped up drone attacks on the Kerch bridge, causing a partial collapse, while Russia has pledged to rebuild the structure stronger. Russian forces have struck Odesa, killing four civilians, and a separate Russian strike killed a Ukrainian mother, an athlete and a drone operator. High casualty levels persist, with 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP. The conflict remains concentrated in occupied Crimea and southern Ukraine, driven by ongoing Russian military operations and Ukrainian retaliatory strikes.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli forces have launched a ground operation beyond the Yellow Line in central Gaza, prompting civilians to flee shelters, while Israeli settlers shot a 72‑year-old Palestinian woman in the West Bank. An Israeli woman contracted rabies, the first case reported in 2024, and Israeli firms face a quiet boycott as banks tighten credit. Sanctions have been imposed on eight Israeli construction firms building settlements in the West Bank, and the government has frozen the E1 settlement tender process. 21,440 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran has expanded its attacks, striking a U.S. air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain with drones and missiles, while also claiming mines hit five ships in the Hormuz Strait. The United States responded with airstrikes on Iranian missile launch sites on Qeshm Island and on vessels in the Gulf of Oman, citing self-defence. A whistleblower alleges the deadly drone strike in Kuwait could have been avoided, adding a new dimension of internal criticism to the conflict. 123 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthis have taken control of the Bab al-Mandeb strait and nearby positions after Yemeni government forces withdrew, moving within about 60 km of Aden. Saudi Arabia dismissed its coalition commander as anti-Houthi forces pulled back from the strait and other key areas, while Saudi-backed forces have intensified attacks on Houthi positions, hitting dozens of military sites. The Yemeni parliament passed a law designating the Houthis as terrorists, raising concerns about a resurgence by southern separatists. Reuters reports Saudi Arabia is preparing a Yemen campaign that could last into 2027. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
Israeli forces are expanding operations in southern Syria, threatening new territory in Syria, Lebanon and Gaza, while Syrian security personnel have been killed in a Damascus countryside attack and in a Jaramana raid that also wounded four others. Christian leaders condemned recent attacks on their community, and the UN deputy relief chief warned that Syrians cannot afford more instability. The Syrian security officer killed on the coast was another casualty in the widening violence. The UCDP recorded 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iraqi security forces have redeployed to Jurf al-Nasr and Jurf al-Sakhar to confront the Kataib Hezbollah militia and enforce a crackdown on oil smuggling, with Prime Minister Al-Zaidi threatening forceful removal. An IRGC commander arrived in Iraq for talks amid rising tensions with Kataib Hezbollah, while an Iran-backed militia tortured an environmental activist protecting marshes and detained a former PMF commander. Iraqi fighter jets struck ISIS remnants in Anbar and launched two airstrikes against the group in the same province. The government also ordered security steps for the Jurf al-Sakhar oil pipeline and referred pipeline violations to the judiciary. 396 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Sudanese army and allied forces have claimed heavy losses inflicted on RSF near the Chad border while continuing advances toward RSF strongholds in West Kordofan and the Blue Nile. RSF drone strikes have killed at least 1,630 civilians, hitting markets, hospitals and fuel sites, prompting Amnesty International to call for war crimes investigations into attacks on El Obeid. Sudanese courts have sentenced RSF chief Hemedti and 13 others to death in absentia, and a Sudanese court sentenced the head of the RSF to death in absentia. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:
Drone strikes have become a major source of fatalities, with Sudan drones responsible for nearly three quarters of war deaths this year and South Sudan accusing Sudan of a drone attack that killed scores in a disputed area. A priest who fled South Sudan was murdered in Birmingham, while a pastor was jailed in South Sudan for performing a Christian song with musical instruments. The government screened out 54 children from a police recruitment drive and SPLM Jonglei chairperson candidates began their race without primaries in Pigi County, where a chairperson was injured in a road incident. Protesters demanded inclusion in the UNISFA mandate drafting, and UCDP recorded two battle-related deaths in 2024.

item.description:
Ethiopian and Eritrean forces are massing troops along their shared border, raising fears of a new war. Clashes between Ethiopian militia and Somali Federalist Party supporters in Moyale have displaced thousands and prompted EU emergency aid of about Sh80 million. A drone strike near Badme wounded four civilians, while a study reports high rates of suicidal behavior among conflict-affected Ethiopian high schoolers. The conflict has already caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:

In Mali, the army rescued 24 personnel and received Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters and an Il-76 transport, while 300 Russian mercenaries were killed. A Protestant missionary abducted in Niger was released and thousands of Arab nomads were ordered to leave southeast Niger. Al-Qaeda and ISIS fighting is escalating in the Sahel and Burkina Faso is targeting critics in exile. The conflict caused 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad and Niger have approved a 5 km cross-border military pursuit to combat terrorism, extending security operations beyond national borders. The African Bar Association has called for mediation in the Anglophone crisis, while the UN Human Rights Committee released findings on Cameroon’s situation. Activist Agbor Balla warned that a decade of bloodshed still prevents children from safely returning to school in the conflict zones. item.title: Myanmar's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The junta has destroyed bridges in Arakan, moved west of the Sittaung River, and is planning a 108‑kilometre fence on the Bangladesh border while airstrikes hit a displacement camp in Rakhine. In Sagaing, junta forces killed 11 people as Starlink outages isolated communities and health-care facilities continued to be attacked in October 2026. Gold revenues now fund resistance groups and Myanmar-linked arsenic pollution is driving a clean-water scramble in Thailand. The UN's top court will soon rule on the Rohingya genocide case, a verdict that Rohingya refugees are pinning their hopes on, and 2,332 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

Haiti formalised a security pact with El Salvador and deployed Salvadoran troops who have engaged in combat against gangs, prompting both supportive and oppositional street protests. Mexican army units are engaging in street shootouts in Jalisco and other states while hunting cartel gangsters, and a police helicopter opened fire on a cartel chase near the U.S. border, killing a 7-year-old girl. An ICE officer in Maine shot and killed an immigrant after expressing hatred of immigrants. Antonio Oseguera Cervantes, brother of Jalisco New Generation co-founder El Mencho, was sentenced to 22 years in a U.S. prison for a drug-trafficking plot. 37 battle-related deaths in 1996, according to UCDP.
